source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.
prompt:
You are assisting with a scholarly experiment in structural literary analysis.

TASK: Write an ORIGINAL short prose passage in English, set in the target scenario below. It must be
a HOMEOSYNTACTIC transposition of a hidden source: hold the source's syntactic form at the level
specified below while inventing entirely new words and moving the content into the target
scenario. It is NOT a paraphrase or a translation.

FORM TARGET (hold this). Reproduce, period by period, the CLAUSE-NESTING SCHEMA below --- an indented tree in which each line is a clause (main / relative / adverbial / complement / coordinate) and indentation marks subordination (a clause indented under another is embedded in it). Hold the SAME nesting: the same clauses, each embedded under the same kind of parent clause, to the same depth. The WORD ORDER and the words themselves are entirely yours; only the clause-embedding tree is fixed.
Reproduce it for all 10 periods, in this order:
Period 1 (about 8 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
Period 2 (about 29 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - open complement (infinitive)
    - adverbial clause
Period 3 (about 3 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
Period 4 (about 15 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - relative/adnominal clause
Period 5 (about 11 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - adverbial clause
      - relative/adnominal clause
Period 6 (about 9 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - relative/adnominal clause
      - open complement (infinitive)
Period 7 (about 12 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - adverbial clause
Period 8 (about 18 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
Period 9 (about 19 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - relative/adnominal clause
      - finite complement clause
        - open complement (infinitive)
          - relative/adnominal clause
Period 10 (about 9 words) clause-nesting schema:
  - main clause
    - finite complement clause

TARGET SCENARIO --- render the content here (in your own words):
  - a supermarket checkout line at a busy hour
  - the conveyor belt, the barcode scanner, the bagging area, the card reader
  - the cashier and a shopper; a cart, a divider bar, a receipt
  - another shopper crowding from behind; a small friction over space in the queue
  - the register of retail routine: beeps, the total announced, loyalty-card prompts

REQUIREMENTS --- both hold together:
1. CLAUSE NESTING PRESERVED --- the same clause-embedding tree per period (which clause embeds in which, to the same depth), in any word order and words you choose.
2. COHERENT --- one continuous, fully sensible passage in the target scenario; new lexicon,
   no trace of any source content.

Write modern, natural English. Produce the 10 periods in order as continuous prose --- no
numbering, no headings. Output ONLY the passage: no preamble, no self-audit.

gens.text:
At checkout, swiftly scanned were groceries,
while impatiently waited others,
behind whom stood a hurried customer,
who nearly bumped into the divider bar,
as methodically rang up items the cashier did,
until loudly beeped the machine, declaring the total,
prompting the insertion of a loyalty card,
after which neatly packed were purchases,
into bags slid through by a helper,
with a receipt handed finally.

Alice waited impatiently as the queue moved forward slowly, hoping to finish her purchase before the store closed, despite Barbara nudging impatiently from behind with her cart, insisting that she could not wait any longer for Alice to bag her items, so the cashier, observing the tension, suggested using the divider bar to separate their spaces on the conveyor belt, thus allowing both transactions to proceed more smoothly without any further delay, even though the system beeped continuously, announcing each item's price as it passed through the barcode scanner, prompting them both to insert their loyalty cards at the card reader, finally issuing a receipt that detailed the total amount spent, and indicating that Alice had just enough time left to grab a quick snack from the adjacent café, after which she would surely leave the bustling supermarket premises with a sense of relief.

Alice stood in the aisle,
waiting to pay her items,
as the scanner beeped behind the glass,
noticing the divider bar nudging forward,
for she saw Brenda press closer from behind,
while the conveyor belt hummed quietly beneath her basket,
though the cashier typed swiftly, eyes scanning the screen,
until the total was announced with a polite smile,
and Alice reached for her card, hesitating,
yet the machine requested a PIN instead,
which prompted her to remember where she last swiped,
before she inserted it carefully, watching the digits turn,
to confirm the transaction complete with a chime,
and handed over the receipt,
amidst the steady rhythm of shopping trolleys gliding past,
where another customer joined the line,
feeling the familiar tension of queue dynamics,
as the beeps continued their rhythmic tune,
marking each step of the checkout dance,
until Alice stepped aside, her bags neatly packed,
to let the next in line proceed smoothly,
with the register echoing its final prompt,
as she left, clutching her receipt and bags.

Alice waited impatiently for her turn at the counter,
hoping to quickly finish her shopping before the store closed,
despite having just started her round,
as the steady stream of customers slowed down her progress,
since every item needed scanning carefully,
each one tagged with a unique code,
that the machine read swiftly,
confirming prices one by one,
while she juggled a cart filled with essentials,
placing items through the divider bar,
into plastic bags neatly arranged,
the cashier prompted for a loyalty card,
after the final beep signified the end of her total,
another shopper nudged gently from behind,
seeking more space in the crowded queue,
and Alice handed over her cash smoothly,
receiving back a receipt as evidence of purchase,
having navigated the complex routine of retail transactions,
she stepped away with a sigh of relief,
feeling the weight of her grocery bags,
knowing the next step was loading them safely into her car.

Alice waited impatiently for her turn at the checkout, wishing the queue would move faster.
To swiftly pay for her items, she hoped that everyone ahead of her would not linger.
Beside her, the conveyor belt gleamed under the scanner's light.
Behind the divider bar, her cart held essentials like bread and milk.
While the cashier scanned each item, her anticipation grew with each beep.
A fellow shopper's urgency pressed from behind, causing a minor skirmish for space.
As the total was announced, the bagger began to arrange groceries into bags.
Despite the crowd, Alice kept her focus on the transaction at hand.
Forgetting about the loyalty card, a reminder whispered softly, urging her to swipe.
With the final step completed, she accepted the receipt, ready to leave.

Alice waited impatiently in the bustling aisle,
to swiftly deposit her items across the scanner,
as the machine beeped rhythmically beside her,
while behind her, Bob nudged urgently forward,
for the divider bar had grown cramped with products,
that were now being scanned by the diligent cashier,
who carefully packed each item into neat sacks,
when suddenly the system paused, prompting loyalty,
which required Alice to swipe her card precisely,
and thus completed the transaction smoothly, indeed.

Alice waited impatiently for her turn at the checkout line, where the conveyor belt whirred steadily, preparing to scan the barcode of her groceries.
While she wished the cashier would move faster, the machine behind the counter beeped methodically as it processed each item, drawing her gaze to the pile of goods neatly stacked on the belt.
The divider bar between counters caught her attention, its presence a silent reminder of the space dividing her from the other side.
As she stood there, holding her cart steady, another shopper nudged her slightly from behind, their urgency adding a slight tension to the air around her.
In front of her, the cashier handled a customer's card smoothly, the card reader accepting it with a soft chime, a routine dance of numbers and plastic.
Behind the bustling activity of scanning and bagging, a small argument simmered about the division of a shared cart, voices low but unmistakable.
Across the aisle, a shopper fumbled with their receipt, their fingers tracing over the printed lines of discounts and taxes.
When Alice finally reached the end of the queue, she placed her items onto the scale, the familiar ritual of weight measurement a comforting constant amid the chaos.
Inside the plastic bag being prepared for her, a small divider nestled among the fruits, its function clear though unspoken, keeping everything in place.
She paid, watching the amount adjust on the screen before signing away the expense with a quick swipe of her finger, completing her transaction with a final beep signaling closure.

Alice waited her turn at the bustling checkout,
to pay for her items while the scanner hummed steadily,
the conveyor belt moved swiftly past the divider bar,
where groceries piled up neatly awaiting their fate,
as she held out a bottle towards the barcode,
which the cashier scanned with practiced ease,
after swiping her loyalty card through the reader,
she placed the receipt in a pocket,
another customer nudged slightly from behind,
while the bagger prepared her goods meticulously,
at the end of the line, the total was announced loudly,
causing everyone to pause momentarily,
and Alice felt a gentle push urging her forward,
from the person in the queue behind her,
though the store’s automated prompts played softly,
reminding shoppers about their points and rewards,
each beep signaling another item processed,
until finally, her turn came to receive her bags,
with a polite smile, the cashier handed them over,
and Alice stepped back, ready to navigate the crowded aisle.

The checkout line buzzed with the steady rhythm of shopping carts rolling toward the scanner. To swiftly tally the items, she aimed the laser at each barcode,  
hoping to reduce the wait,  
while the shopper ahead adjusted her cart against the divider bar.  
Beside her, the conveyor belt carried a pile of groceries,  
which belonged to a customer who was carefully placing them for bagging.  
Nearby, the bagger reached for plastic bags,  
which were to contain the scanned goods,  
so that they could be packed efficiently.  
Behind, another patron nudged forward,  
feeling the tension over personal space in the crowded aisle.  
At the register, the machine hummed,  
as it processed payments,  
showing the running total on its screen.  
Next to it, the credit card slot invited swipes,  
from customers holding cards in anticipation.  
A receipt printer clicked, spitting out the slip,  
which showed details of purchases made that day.  
Near the exit, a final beep signaled the end of transactions,  
completing yet another round of retail routine,  
where every item checked marked another sale concluded.

At the bustling market queue, the scanner whirred,
to swiftly tally the trolley's contents while,
beside, a pusher pressed forward, nearly nudging,
the divider bar between us, as the belt conveyed,
our parcels past the beep of every priced item,
which, noted neatly, prompted a digital display,
showing sums that, once confirmed, invited a swipe,
of a card for club members, whose perks, silently,
awaited our acknowledgment, as we sorted our bags,
under the watchful glance of the cashier.
